must_remember: In a plane progressive wave, all particles execute simple harmonic motion with the same amplitude and frequency.
The phase changes continuously along the direction of wave propagation according to $\Delta \phi = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda} \Delta x$.
Wave velocity depends on the elastic and inertial properties of the medium, whereas particle velocity is the instantaneous velocity of a medium particle in SHM.
The relation between particle velocity $v_p$ and wave velocity $v$ is given by $v_p = -(\text{slope of displacement curve}) \times v$.
The intensity of a progressive wave is proportional to the square of its amplitude and the square of its frequency: $I \propto A^2 f^2$.

glossary.meaning: A wave that transfers energy and momentum from one point of the medium to another without permanent bulk transport of matter.
Spatial angular frequency defined as $k = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}$, representing phase change per unit distance.
The instantaneous velocity of a specific medium particle executing simple harmonic motion, given by $v_p = \frac{\partial y}{\partial t}$.
The speed at which the phase of disturbance travels through the medium, given by $v = f\lambda = \frac{\omega}{k}$.
Average energy transmitted per unit time per unit area normal to the direction of wave propagation, measured in $\text{W m}^{-2}$.
